introduction: This third Sunday of Advent is Gaudete Sunday, and rose vestments may be worn. Isaiah sees the desert bloom, and the blind, deaf and lame healed. In the Gospel, John the Baptist, in prison, sends his disciples to ask Jesus, Are you the one who is to come? Jesus points to his works of healing. Saint James urges us to be patient like the farmer. Let us rejoice, for the Lord is near.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, the Lord comes to save us. With joy, let us bring him our prayers.
intentions: For the Church: that she may rejoice in the Lord and show his saving works to the world. Let us pray to the Lord.
For the sick, the blind, the deaf and the disabled: that they may experience the healing love of Christ. Let us pray to the Lord.
For prisoners, especially those imprisoned for their faith: that they may find hope, as John did. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who are discouraged or impatient: that they may wait for the Lord with the patience of the farmer. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may recognize Christ in his works and not be offended by his ways. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: God of joy, you make the desert bloom and heal the broken. Strengthen our weak hands and fearful hearts, and fill us with joy at the coming of your Son. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: Are you the one who is to come?
reflection.body:
Today the Church pauses in Advent to rejoice. Isaiah's prophecy is full of joy: "The wilderness and the dry land will be glad. The desert will rejoice and blossom like a rose." He speaks to everyone who is afraid: "Be strong! Don't be afraid! Behold, your God will come." When God comes, "the eyes of the blind will be opened, and the ears of the deaf will be unstopped. Then the lame man will leap like a deer." And "sorrow and sighing will flee away."

In the Gospel, John the Baptist is in prison. The fiery prophet who announced that the one coming would bring judgment now hears reports of a Messiah who heals and forgives. Perhaps he is puzzled. He sends his disciples to ask Jesus: "Are you he who comes, or should we look for another?"

Jesus does not answer with a title. He points to what is happening: "the blind receive their sight, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised up, and the poor have good news preached to them." These are the signs Isaiah foretold. And he adds, "Blessed is he who finds no occasion for stumbling in me." God's ways are not always what we expect.

Then Jesus praises John: "among those who are born of women there has not arisen anyone greater than John the Baptizer."

Saint James speaks to all who wait: "Be patient therefore, brothers, until the coming of the Lord. Behold, the farmer waits for the precious fruit of the earth." He adds, "Establish your hearts, for the coming of the Lord is at hand."

This week, look for the signs of Christ's presence: healing, mercy, good news for the poor. Be part of them yourself. And rejoice: the Lord is near.
